summary: Measured with a 3s GPU sampler: Vision idle on landing = 410 MB dedicated VRAM; after opening a 161-asset project and scrolling it = 2111 MB peak, resting 1858.2 MB byte-identical for 13 minutes with zero decay. Entering the history workspace drops it to 404 MB, proving the memory is fully releasable and that only grid teardown releases it. Root cause is the promote observer in MpiGalleryGrid.js: it ignores !isIntersecting and unobserves after promoting, so every video card that scrolls past keeps a <video preload=auto> for the life of the grid. _removeHoverVideo already exists and does the right teardown; its five call sites are all content-change paths, never scroll-out or visibility. Fabio's framing: the problem is not idle usage in the abstract, it is the UI holding VRAM the user needs for a generation.

todo -> doing. Building the release primitive on Fabio's go. Scope is his two triggers only: release the gallery's promoted hover videos when the gallery stops being the visible surface, and when a generation is dispatched. Wiring turned out to need no cross-file plumbing - Overlays.onDepthChange in MpiGalleryGrid is already the single choke point MPI-570 built for exactly this question ('depth 0 -> 1 IS the gallery stopped being the visible surface', with Flow / Model Manager / Flow Library / History all routing through it), and generation:started + generation:complete + state.generationQueueCount are the pair notificationService already uses for a drained queue. Owning MpiGalleryGrid.js, types.js, a new desktop spec, docs/gallery.md and UNRELEASED.md. Scroll-out demotion and the engine's separate idle-unload are deliberately NOT in this card.

Acceptance 1 amended: the release primitive is INTERNAL, not exposed on instance.el. The card was written expecting a public releaseMedia()/resumeMedia() pair, but both callers turned out to live inside the grid itself - Overlays.onDepthChange and the generation events are all subscribed in its own setup - so a public method would have been API with no consumer. Recorded rather than quietly satisfied, because the criterion as written would otherwise read as unmet. Implementation is green: 751/751 unit, and the new tests/desktop/gallery-media-release.spec.js passes and was mutation-tested twice - removing the demote sweep goes red (expected 0, got 4) and neutering the _mediaHolds guard in _promoteVideo goes red the same way, so both halves are load-bearing rather than one masking the other.

Trigger C added on Fabio's go, and the measurement is why. With ONLY the overlay and generation holds live, the post-fix tour showed the holds firing exactly as designed - Vision dropped to ~500-670 MB three times in 90s against a pre-fix baseline that only ever dropped in the History workspace - but sitting idle in the gallery still rested at 1976 MB against the pre-fix 1858. Not a bug in the holds: neither an overlay nor a generation is present when a user simply sits in a scrolled gallery, so nothing held and every decoder came back. The two problems turned out to be different (VRAM at dispatch vs VRAM at rest) and only the first was in scope. Fabio also established the resume sweep is correct by observation: returning to the gallery WITHOUT scrolling stays cheap because _resumeMedia only promotes the visible band - his 1976 came from deliberately scrolling to the bottom each time, which re-promoted everything through the observer. Trigger C is a second IntersectionObserver at 600px demoting on !isIntersecting, against the promote observer's 200px. Three mutations now, three reds: killing the demote sweep, neutering the _mediaHolds guard, and gutting the demoteObserver callback each go red on their own assertion, so no half masks another. 751/751 unit, both spec cases green, lint clean.

doing -> done. Measured on the real 161-asset project with the engine off, so the app is measured alone: resting VRAM 1858.2 MB -> 738.2 MB (-1120 MB, -60%), peak 2111 -> 961 MB, flat for the final 90s. The 3455 MB spike that appeared with the overlay+generation holds alone is gone, because the gallery under a flow is now bounded. 751/751 unit, 31/31 desktop, eslint clean, board validates. Three mutations, three reds, all reverted - and that check earned its keep twice: the trigger-C case first passed against a fixture overflowing by only 361px, less than DEMOTE_MARGIN_PX, so the demote could never fire and it was green for the wrong reason. NOT measured, and recorded as such in validation.md: Vision's VRAM at the instant a real generation dispatches. Trigger B is proven by spec + mutation + sharing the release path the measured overlay trigger uses, but the live number needs the engine up and a generation run, and the engine was deliberately off for every measurement. Closed on the evidence; reopen if that number is wanted. Follow-up raised as MPI-632.
